key_insight: SparseDecoding aligns pruning with autoregressive decoding tokens instead of fixed natural-text calibration, improving accuracy and inference speed for LLMs.
engineering_relevance: It targets the memory-bound decoding bottleneck with a pruning-and-kernel co-design that can deliver real end-to-end speedups on GPU.
method: Collect layer-wise activations during dense-model autoregressive generation and use them to build decoding-aware calibration matrices.
Prune with a Hessian-guided objective matched to generated-token distributions rather than pre-collected text.
Use an optimized N:M sparse matrix-vector kernel with bitmask indexing and fixed-step traversal for decoding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, and Qwen3-14B/32B, with consistent gains on long-form generation and up to 1.48x wall-clock decoding speedup on A100 GPUs.
watch_item: Speedups depend on an optimized SpMV kernel and hardware support; if sparse decoding paths are not well-implemented, the benefit may be limited.
paper_title: SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference
